nodes.label: app-db-01
web-app-01
web-app-03
Public-facing web server received exploit requests against the login endpoint before external TLS traffic began.
WAF telemetry also showed generic scanner payloads blocked earlier in the same window.
The web server resolved cdn-auth-check.net shortly after the exploit attempts.
Seed JA4 alert matched a possible web-shell beacon over TLS.
The same web server reconnected to the same external infrastructure after the seed alert.
A web-shell file named shell.aspx appeared under /var/www/html/.cache after the exploit traffic.
PowerShell launcher executed under w3wp and reached the same temporary web cache path.
Credential-store access from the web worker account followed the PowerShell launcher.
SMB connection from web-app-01 to app-db-01 followed the web-shell and PowerShell activity.
The database server resolved the same rare C2 domain after the SMB connection from web-app-01.
app-db-01 contacted the original external infrastructure after the lateral movement signal.
Remote service creation from web-app-01 to app-db-01 appeared after app-db-01 contacted the beacon infrastructure.
A second web server resolved a sibling domain on the same IP, but only as a single weak candidate signal.
web-app-03 also reached the same hosting IP through a scanner telemetry vendor domain.
A planned hotfix deployment started after the suspicious chain and may explain later service restarts.
Script block logging was disabled on web-app-01, limiting command detail behind the PowerShell launcher.
